statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting Mettl3 weakened the deposition of several heterochromatin marks at METTL3-targeted IAPs and increased IAP transcription.
statements.evidence: Knockout of Mettl3 impairs the deposition of multiple heterochromatin marks onto METTL3-targeted IAPs, and upregulates IAP transcription
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this result of the Mettl3 knockout: impaired heterochromatin marks at targeted IAPs together with upregulated IAP transcription.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The m6A reader YTHDC1 binds the methylated IAP transcripts, interacts with METTL3, and strengthens the association of METTL3 with chromatin.
statements.evidence: These m 6 A-marked transcripts are bound by the m 6 A reader YTHDC1, which interacts with METTL3 and in turn promotes the association of METTL3 with chromatin.
statements.note: Each element of the statement - YTHDC1 binding the m6A-marked transcripts, interacting with METTL3, and promoting METTL3's chromatin association - is stated in the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mettl3-knockout mouse embryonic stem cells fail to differentiate into the three embryonic germ layers.
statements.evidence: Here we show that METTL3 regulates mouse embryonic stem-cell heterochromatin, the integrity of which is critical for silencing retroviral elements and for mammalian development 5 .
statements.note: The abstract notes that heterochromatin integrity matters for mammalian development in general, but reports no differentiation experiment on Mettl3-knockout cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: METTL3 physically binds the H3K9 tri-methyltransferase SETDB1 and its cofactor TRIM28, and it is needed for their localization to IAPs.
statements.evidence: METTL3 also interacts physically with the histone 3 lysine 9 (H3K9) tri-methyltransferase SETDB1 and its cofactor TRIM28, and is important for their localization to IAPs.
statements.note: The abstract states both the physical interaction with SETDB1 and TRIM28 and METTL3's importance for bringing them to IAPs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Human senescent cells switch on HERVK (HML-2), the most recently integrated human ERV family, transcribing its viral genes and producing retrovirus-like particles.
statements.evidence: In human senescent cells, we found that HERVK (HML-2), the most recently integrated human ERVs, are unlocked to transcribe viral genes and produce retrovirus-like particles (RVLPs).
statements.note: The abstract reports this finding in senescent human cells, including that HERVK is the most recently integrated human ERV family.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Retrovirus-like particles released by senescent cells insert new HERVK copies into the genomes of the young cells they enter.
statements.evidence: These HERVK RVLPs constitute a transmissible message to elicit senescence phenotypes in young cells, which can be blocked by neutralizing antibodies.
statements.note: The abstract reports that the particles transmit senescence phenotypes to young cells but says nothing about whether they create new genomic insertions there.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Repressing ERVs eased cellular senescence and tissue degeneration, and to a limited extent organismal aging.
statements.evidence: Their repression alleviates cellular senescence and tissue degeneration and, to some extent, organismal aging.
statements.note: The abstract states that ERV repression alleviates senescence and tissue degeneration, and organismal aging only to some extent.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ERV activation was detected beyond cultured cells: in organs of aged primates and mice, and in tissues and serum from elderly humans.
statements.evidence: The activation of ERVs was also observed in organs of aged primates and mice as well as in human tissues and serum from the elderly.
statements.note: The abstract lists exactly these settings in which ERV activation was also observed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IscB cuts double-stranded DNA under the guidance of a single noncoding RNA, and it works for genome editing in human cells.
statements.evidence: We found that IscB uses a single noncoding RNA for RNA-guided cleavage of double-stranded DNA and can be harnessed for genome editing in human cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports both the single-noncoding-RNA-guided DNA cleavage by IscB and its use for editing human cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Combining evolutionary analysis, RNA sequencing and biochemistry, the study traced CRISPR-Cas9 systems to IS200/IS605 transposons, placing the transposon nucleases earlier in that lineage.
statements.evidence: Using evolutionary analysis, RNA sequencing, and biochemical experiments, we reconstructed the evolution of CRISPR-Cas9 systems from IS200/IS605 transposons.
statements.note: The abstract states that these three approaches were used to reconstruct the evolution of CRISPR-Cas9 from IS200/IS605 transposons, which makes the transposon systems the earlier form.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TnpB, a second protein encoded by IS200/IS605 transposons, also cleaves DNA under RNA guidance.
statements.evidence: We also demonstrate the RNA-guided nuclease activity of TnpB, another IS200/IS605 transposon-encoded protein and the likely ancestor of Cas12 endonucleases.
statements.note: The abstract reports demonstrating RNA-guided nuclease activity for TnpB, another IS200/IS605 transposon-encoded protein.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: OMEGA nucleases are compact enough to be packaged into adeno-associated viral vectors more easily than Cas9.
statements.evidence: This work reveals a widespread class of transposon-encoded RNA-guided nucleases, which we name OMEGA (obligate mobile element–guided activity), with strong potential for developing as biotechnologies.
statements.note: The abstract claims biotechnological potential for the OMEGA class but never mentions protein size, vector packaging, or any comparison with Cas9 on those grounds.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumors carry TE cryptic promoter-activation events have shorter overall survival.
statements.evidence: However, the prevalence and impact of TE onco-exaptation events across cancer types are poorly characterized.
statements.note: The abstract names the impact of onco-exaptation across cancer types as the gap it addresses, but it reports no patient-survival analysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 7,769 tumors and 625 normal datasets from 15 cancer types, the survey found 129 TE cryptic promoter-activation events involving 106 oncogenes in 3,864 tumors.
statements.evidence: Here, we analyzed 7,769 tumors and 625 normal datasets from 15 cancer types, identifying 129 TE cryptic promoter-activation events involving 106 oncogenes across 3,864 tumors.
statements.note: These are the counts the abstract gives for the datasets analyzed and the events, oncogenes and tumors identified.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting the AluJb element caused a complete loss of LIN28B expression, while shifting DNA methylation changed the activity of that promoter.
statements.evidence: the genetic deletion of the TE eliminated oncogene expression, while dynamic DNA methylation modulated promoter activity
statements.note: For the AluJb-LIN28B candidate the abstract reports that deleting the TE eliminated oncogene expression and that DNA methylation modulated promoter activity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study characterizes the global profile of TE onco-exaptation and presents it as a prevalent mechanism of promiscuous oncogene activation and tumorigenesis.
statements.evidence: Collectively, our results characterize the global profile of TE onco-exaptation and highlight this prevalent phenomenon as an important mechanism for promiscuous oncogene activation and ultimately tumorigenesis.
statements.note: This restates the abstract's own summary of what its results establish.
